Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
Friday bounced, but the bounce changed nobody's mind. QQQ printed a green candle (+1.40% to 656.10) after Thursday's −6.49% capitulation, SPY added 0.31% to 735.29, IWM 0.99% to 273.67, and TLT was flat at 81.92 — yet every index still sits below its 30-week line, and only SPY and IWM are even above their 50-week EMAs, by 1.56% and 0.07%. Prof supplies the structure: the Nasdaq is now firmly below its 200-day SMA, so on any meaningful bounce a retest of that average from below is the first major resistance he will watch — and he asks Grok to study 25 years of breakdowns below the 200-day for how often the first retest came and how long it took. He also supplies the NVDA verdict: roughly 22% off the highs, and the trendline that had supported the entire move is finally lost — the next phase is time, not a straight trip back to highs: consolidate, build a base, establish new support. His MU chart adds the week's other level: the 50-weekly SMA, first tested since the June 2025 reclaim, with a stop at a weekly close below 650 — Thursday's low printed exactly 650.00 and Friday closed 690.00. Venu supplies the checklist and the rotation: his five bottom signs count 2 of 5 — capitulation volume (QQQ −6.5% on ~3x volume) and fear spike (VIX +70%, 3rd-largest ever) are checked, while selling slowing, leaders holding up and a follow-through day are not — and his next-phase call is that leadership rotates toward the hyperscalers MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN and META, on cloud growth, cash flow and a possible CapEx-growth slowdown lifting free cash flow, while the semiconductor leaders go through “Stage 4 declines” (his words) and take time to rebuild. He also supplies the two relative-strength names, Unity and AppLovin, both printing PEG candles — without saying which is the breakout attempt and which is the reversal. DiCarlo supplies the hard levels: MU has to hold $700 — it didn't, closing 690.00 — or he sees another 30% drop over the next couple of months; BE is back at its long-term Smart Money Zone and already bouncing, with ATHs within 6–12 months 70% of the time from this zone; AAOI is down 70% since his August sell-off call and approaching the strongest support in his system. Enrich supplies the valuation case and the trap: CRDO is an “asymmetrical opportunity through 2030” — revenue up 115% while the forward P/E fell 80% to 15.4x — and his weekend pattern is to trap late bears from Friday, then trap bulls Monday morning, and repeat. He also flags the Jensen headline (US officials believing the Nvidia CEO had a “romantic relationship” with a Chinese spy) with no call attached. Remz supplies the discipline: early-morning rips in a bearish environment are enticing but best resisted, days like Friday are for observing, and SNDK down 80 with MU down 50 tells him nothing is simple about the trend. iain supplies the weekend: a reminder not to get so obsessed with the markets that you forget to live. Sean supplies nothing new — no posts in this window. Your process gives no confirmed breakout today: U is the only constructive watch, sitting exactly on its 52-week high with Venu's relative-strength call behind it, and the rest of the board is tests to survive — MU between Prof's 650 stop and DiCarlo's failed 700, NVDA below a broken trendline, GOOGL's $270 test still live, APP 1.68% under its 30-week line, and the hyperscalers still split between above-average (MSFT, AMZN) and below (GOOGL, META). The discipline is in the framing: watch U's high, MU's 650/700 lines and the Nasdaq 200-day retest, wait for Venu's follow-through day, and do not chase a one-day green candle.

  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended/avoid). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. The stage pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) is the only place a stage label appears; it is kept out of the prose and the setup badges, and traders' own quoted words are exempt.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels. APP merges its 30-week MA trigger with the 50-week EMA into one row (0.71% apart); U merges its 30-week MA and 50-week EMA supports into one row. MU's invalidation is Prof's trader-stated 650, not a chart anchor.
  • Trader charts: five embedded this edition, all retrieved from the traders' visible posts and verified by viewing the image: Enrich's CRDO valuation infographic (revenue $223M→$479M, forward P/E 76.9x→15.4x); Prof's MU weekly chart (50 SMA 660.15, week's low 650.00); Prof's NVDA weekly chart (trendline break, “Lost it”, −22.45%); Prof's QQQ daily chart (Thursday's red candle vs Friday's green); Venu's bottom-signs infographic (5 signs, 2 of 5 checked as of Nov 5). DiCarlo's MU, BE and AAOI posts link to X videos, not charts, so no trader chart is embedded for those rows — the video format is stated in their panels.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line's endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all computable lines passed within 0.5%. The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only.
